items.text: SEASON 4 · EPISODE 11 · BOSS LEVEL · DRAFT  Broadcast control-room cascade · Level 2  Kestrel Valley Media, 10:58 p.m. A storm is flooding the valley; the late bulletin is the only news most people will hear tonight. Master control is alarming, the anchor's audio is missing on air, and Felix — the only licensed engineer for the transmitter — is an hour away.  ⚑ CH-01 · BOSS-01: five physics challenges, a signal trace and the calls that aren't yours to make — on the clock. Fail anything and the run starts over. The edge of the screen glows yellow under pressure, red when time is short or the run fails, green when you clear it; it pulses no faster than once a second, and holds steady if you prefer reduced motion.

bubbles.text: Everything, at once. Where do we start?
Where the signal starts. Then one thing at a time — and nothing that isn't ours.

items.caption: Five modes, one clock, no second chances inside a run.

items.alt: The alarm light turns red. The flood alert's in. Can the anchor say it in his own words?

bubbles.text: The flood alert's in. Can the anchor say it in his own words?
No. Verbatim. It's the emergency managers' message.

items.caption: Trace · hear · see · reach · build · record. The boss isn't the fault — it's the pressure to cut a corner.

lines.text: One check per stage. If it fails, we start over from the top — and we'll know why.
Then we start again. That's the job: until it passes, and we can prove it.

items.label: **Boss level: The Storm Desk.** Clear every stage in one run to open the next season. Fail anything and you start again from the top.

items.alt: The alarm light fades to green. The bulletin goes out whole: the alert verbatim, the anchor clean, the loudness right, the reporters' radio mics clear. Felix calls from the…
narration: The bulletin goes out whole: the alert verbatim, the anchor clean, the loudness right, the reporters' radio mics clear. Felix calls from the road: “Don't touch the mountain. You didn't need to.”
items.caption: Cleared. Written down. Handed over.

items.text: FIELD NOTE —  Under pressure, the method doesn't change: trace the signal from source to destination, fix one thing at a time and prove it where the people are, and hand every decision that isn't yours to the person who owns it — the electrician, the rigger and structural engineer, the network owner, security, the emergency managers, the clinical and privacy owners, the artist. Then write it down.
